title: Separate Terraform state files per environment
Set up terraform-module-releaser monorepo with GitHub Actions in terraform-modules
description:
## Overview

Establish `isapp/terraform-modules` as the canonical monorepo for all versioned, DevOps-approved Terraform modules consumed by `terraform` and other consumers across the organization. Use the [terraform-module-releaser](<https://github.com/marketplace/actions/terraform-module-releaser>) GitHub Action to automate per-module semantic versioning and changelog generation via conventional commits.

## Background

All Terraform modules should live in a single, auditable repo (`terraform-modules`). Each module is independently versioned using git tags following the pattern `<provider>/<module-name>/v<semver>` (e.g. `aws/vpc/v1.2.0`). Consumers reference modules via:

```hcl
module "vpc" {
  source = "git::https://github.com/isapp/terraform-modules//aws/vpc?ref=aws/vpc/v1.2.0"
}
```

This approach gives us:

* Per-module changelogs auto-generated from conventional commits
* Immutable version pinning via git tags (no floating references)
* Single source of truth for all approved modules
* PR-based review workflow before any module version is promoted

## Implementation Plan

### Phase 1 — Repo scaffolding and GitHub Action (this issue)

* Add `.github/workflows/terraform-module-releaser.yml` using the `techpivot/terraform-module-releaser` action
* Configure branch protections on `main` to require PR reviews
* Add `CLAUDE.md` with module authoring conventions for AI-assisted development
* Build a first test module (e.g. `aws/s3-bucket`) to validate the release pipeline end-to-end
* Validate that merging a conventional commit PR produces the expected git tag and GitHub release

### Phase 2 — Tooling and quality gates (sub-issues)

* Custom tflint plugin for deterministic module structure validation (see DO sub-issue)
* pre-commit hooks: `terraform fmt`, `terraform validate`, `terraform-docs`
* terraform-docs integration for auto-generating `README.md` inputs/outputs tables per module

### Phase 3 — Module library build-out

* Migrate or author approved modules for common patterns: VPC, security groups, IAM roles, S3, ECS, RDS, etc.
* Each module follows the conventions defined in `CLAUDE.md`

## GitHub Action Configuration

The `terraform-module-releaser` action runs on PRs targeting `main`. It:

1. Detects which module directories changed in the PR
2. Parses conventional commit messages to determine semver bump (feat → minor, fix → patch, breaking → major)
3. On merge to main: creates a git tag and GitHub release per changed module
4. Auto-generates a per-module `CHANGELOG.md`

Workflow file location: `.github/workflows/terraform-module-releaser.yml`

## Repo

* GitHub: [https://github.com/isapp/terraform-modules](<https://github.com/isapp/terraform-modules>)
* Local clone: `/Users/phazeight/repos/terraform/terraform-modules`
* Default branch: `main`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [X] `terraform-module-releaser` GitHub Action workflow is merged to `main` and functional
- [X] At least one test module exists and has been released with a `v1.0.0` tag
- [X] `CLAUDE.md` documents module authoring conventions
- [X] Branch protections require PR + passing checks before merge to `main`
- [X] Sub-issues created for tflint plugin, pre-commit, and terraform-docs

title: Implement `molecules/cidr-map` Terraform subnet allocation module
description:
Build a reusable `molecules/cidr-map` module in `terraform-modules` that takes a single `/16` CIDR block and returns a fully structured subnet allocation map.

## Subnet layout

Given a `/16` input:

* Split into 4 subnet groups (`app`, `data`, `control`, `alb`) at `+6` bits → `/22` each
* Each group further split into 3 AZ subnets (`az1`, `az2`, `az3`) at `+2` bits → `/24` each

Output shape (nested map):

```hcl
{
  cidr    = "10.1.0.0/16"
  app     = { cidr = "10.1.0.0/22", az1 = "10.1.0.0/24", az2 = "10.1.1.0/24", az3 = "10.1.2.0/24" }
  data    = { cidr = "10.1.4.0/22", az1 = "10.1.4.0/24", az2 = "10.1.5.0/24", az3 = "10.1.6.0/24" }
  control = { cidr = "10.1.8.0/22", az1 = "10.1.8.0/24", az2 = "10.1.9.0/24", az3 = "10.1.10.0/24" }
  alb     = { cidr = "10.1.12.0/22", az1 = "10.1.12.0/24", az2 = "10.1.13.0/24", az3 = "10.1.14.0/24" }
}
```

## Design decisions to resolve

* Evaluate whether to use `cloudposse/config/yaml//modules/deepmerge` (as in sandbox prototype) or replace with native Terraform `merge()` — prefer native if complexity doesn't justify the dependency.

## Sub-issues

1. Implement core module (variables, locals, outputs)
2. Add example usage and validate with terraform plan
3. Cut v1.0.0 release tag

title: Implement `cidr-map` core module (variables, locals, outputs)
description:
Create `modules/molecules/cidr-map/` in `terraform-modules` with:

* `variables.tf` — single `cidr` input (string, required)
* `main.tf` — subnet allocation locals using `cidrsubnets()` and `zipmap()`; evaluate native `merge()` vs `cloudposse/deepmerge` for the output map
* `outputs.tf` — single `result` output exposing the nested group→AZ map

Follow repo conventions: alphabetical attributes, `description` on all variables, `>= 1.10` required_version.

title: Add `cidr-map` example usage and validate with terraform plan
description: Create an `examples/cidr-map/` directory that mirrors the sandbox usage (one module call per org account CIDR, outputs for each). Run `terraform init && terraform plan` locally using a relative path source to confirm the module resolves and outputs are correct before tagging.

description:

```hcl

```

Run `terraform init -upgrade && terraform plan` in the example to verify tag resolution before closing the epic.

description:
Port the data layer sandbox prototypes from GitLab into `terraform-modules` as two new molecules:

A data-only module that exposes:

* Hardcoded org-wide account IDs (org-dev, org-stage, org-prod, org-sand, org-name, dev-cloud-loc, dev-loc, stage-loc, pre-prod-loc, prod-loc, org_name_Dev/Stage/Prod/Main)
* Current account context via data sources: `account_id`, `account_alias`, `partition`, `region`

Replaces the existing `gitlab.com/org-name/molecules-data-metadata/aws` source.

## `molecules/data-policies`

A library of reusable `aws_iam_policy_document` outputs consumed by account-level Terraform configs. Depends on `data-metadata`. Covers:

* MFA enforcement (console + CLI)
* Terrassume assume role (+ per-account variants: dev, stage, prod, sand)
* EC2, S3, ECS task execution, ECS tasks, CloudTrail, EventBridge scheduler, EventBridge ECS run, ECR cross-account assume role policies

## Dependency order

`data-metadata` must be tagged before `data-policies` can be implemented (policies module sources metadata).

## Sub-issues

1. Implement `molecules/data-metadata` core module
2. Cut `molecules/data-metadata/v1.0.0` release tag
3. Implement `molecules/data-policies` core module
4. Add `data-policies` example and validate with terraform plan
5. Cut `molecules/data-policies/v1.0.0` release tag

title: Add tflint rule to reject empty locals.tf / helpers.tf in module atoms
description:
## Problem

`tflint` does not flag empty `locals {}` blocks or comment-only `helpers.tf` files committed to module atoms. These files add noise to diffs and module directories without any functional value.

Discovered during gitops atom implementation (PR isapp/terraform-modules#10) — pre-commit hooks (fmt, validate, tflint, docs) all passed with empty files present.

## Options

1. Add a custom rule to `tflint-ruleset-ht` that rejects empty `locals {}` blocks and comment-only files in module directories
2. Add a pre-commit hook (e.g. shell script) that checks for and rejects these files
3. Document convention only — don't create empty files, no enforcement

## Suggested approach

Option 1 or 2. The plan spec called for `locals.tf` and `helpers.tf` in all atoms as a template; we should either enforce they're non-empty or stop generating them by default.

title: Document atom→molecule variable passthrough convention in terraform-modules CLAUDE.md
description:
## Context

During implementation of the `github-managed-repo` molecule, we discovered that `require_code_owner_reviews` was available in the `github-branch-protection` atom but not exposed as a passthrough variable in the molecule. There is no documented convention requiring this, and no tooling to catch the gap.

## Work

* Add convention to `terraform-modules` [CLAUDE.md](<http://CLAUDE.md>): **every variable defined in an atom must be exposed as a passthrough variable in any molecule that calls it** — no molecule should silently suppress an atom's knobs
* Include a short example showing correct passthrough pattern vs. incorrect hardcoding
* Note the specific gap that triggered this: `require_code_owner_reviews` in `github-branch-protection` atom not passed through in `github-managed-repo` molecule

## Acceptance

* [CLAUDE.md](<http://CLAUDE.md>) updated with clear rule + example
* Rule is actionable for both humans and future AI-assisted module authoring

title: [Stretch] Pre-commit script: validate molecule variable coverage against atom inputs
description:
## Context

Follow-up to [DO-350](https://linear.app/twenty/issue/DO-350/document-atommolecule-variable-passthrough-convention-in-terraform). Once the convention is documented, we want tooling to enforce it automatically on every commit.

**tflint is not viable** — the tflint plugin API is single-module scoped with no cross-module analysis capability. Building this as a tflint rule would require writing a separate module graph traversal tool (XL, out of scope).

## Approach

Write a pre-commit hook script (Python or shell) that:

1. Detects molecule modules (e.g. `modules/molecules/*/`)
2. Parses the molecule's `main.tf` to find atom module sources + their input variable assignments
3. For each referenced atom, fetches the atom's `inputs.tf` (local path or cached clone) and enumerates all declared variables
4. Diffs atom variables against molecule passthrough variables — flags any atom variable not exposed in the molecule's `inputs.tf`
5. Emits violations with file + variable name for easy fix

## Notes

* Local relative paths are used during dev; versioned HTTPS refs in committed code — script must handle both
* Only flag missing passthroughs, not variables intentionally hardcoded (may need an escape hatch annotation)

## Acceptance

* Script runs as a pre-commit hook on `terraform-modules`
* Catches the `require_code_owner_reviews` class of gap before merge
* False positive rate is low enough to be practical

title: Analyse named AWS profile pattern in commercial Terraform provider configs
description:
## Background

Every `provider.tf` in `terraform/aws/commercial/` hardcodes a named AWS profile in both the provider block and the S3 backend block. Current pattern:

```hcl
provider "aws" {
  profile = "prod"
  region  = "us-east-1"
}

terraform {
  backend "s3" {
    profile = "prod"
    ...
  }
}
```

Affected files span 17 `provider.tf` files across 8+ accounts with profiles: `dev`, `stg`, `uat`, `prod`, `mgmt`, `security`, `snowplow`, `commercial-main`.

## Objective

Produce a recommendation for removing hardcoded profile names from these files, enabling consistent local dev and CI/CD execution without requiring named profiles in `~/.aws/config`.

## Scope

1. **Inventory** — catalogue all `profile = "..."` occurrences (provider + S3 backend blocks) across all commercial account directories
2. **Risk analysis** — document current risks:
   * Requires every developer to have matching named profiles in `~/.aws/config`
   * CI/CD runners must also maintain the same profile names
   * Drift risk when profile names change or new accounts are onboarded
3. **Alternatives evaluation** — assess options:
   * `AWS_PROFILE` env var (removes hardcoding, still profile-based)
   * `AWS_ROLE_ARN` + assume-role via provider `assume_role` block (profile-free)
   * OIDC/IAM role injection in CI with no local profile required
   * `awsp` wrapper pattern already in use locally
4. **Recommendation** — pick an approach with rationale, covering both local dev workflow and CI/CD
5. **Migration path** — outline the refactor steps as input for follow-on sub-issues

## Out of scope

* Actual refactoring implementation (separate issues after this analysis)
* Non-commercial directories

title: Remove RDS, Lambda rotation, and rds_master_password from stg identity-service module before apply
description:
The stg identity-service module was written with an RDS instance, Lambda rotation, and related resources matching dev/UAT/prod. Per [DO-703](https://linear.app/twenty/issue/DO-703/stg-parity-do-not-stand-up-identity-service-rds-dev-and-stg) investigation, none of these should be created — the identity service uses the platform RDS, not a standalone one.

Strip the following from `acct_x179_stg/services/identity-service/` **before running terraform plan/apply**:

* **Delete** `rds.tf` (aws_db_instance, parameter group, subnet group, security group, ingress rule)
* **Delete** `lambda.tf` (archive_file, aws_lambda_function, lambda_permission, secretsmanager_secret_rotation)
* `secrets.tf` — remove `aws_secretsmanager_secret.db_credentials` only; keep jwt_signing_keys, oidc_idme, oidc_logingov, ssn_hmac_key, missouri_sso_client_secret
* `inputs.tf` — remove `rds_master_password` variable
* `iam.tf` — remove rotation_lambda assume/policy/role/attachment blocks; remove `db_credentials.arn` from `identity_secrets_read` statement
* `outputs.tf` — remove `identity_rds_endpoint` output
* **Delete** `secrets.auto.tfvars` (no longer needed)

After stripping, re-run `terraform plan` and confirm expected resource count drops accordingly (no aws_db_instance, no aws_lambda_function in plan output).

title: Destroy identity-uat RDS — orphaned identity-service instance (Multi-AZ)
description:
Follow-on to [DO-705](https://linear.app/twenty/issue/DO-705/destroy-identity-dev-rds-after-eric-mai-sign-off) (dev destroy, PR #524). `identity-uat` is a Multi-AZ RDS instance confirmed orphaned — 0 `DatabaseConnections` over 7+ days. The identity-service ECS task def routes `HT_IDENTITY_APP_DATABASE_URL` to `platform-uat`, not this instance.

**Two-stage Terraform destroy (same pattern as** [DO-705](https://linear.app/twenty/issue/DO-705/destroy-identity-dev-rds-after-eric-mai-sign-off)**):**

### Stage 1 — Disable deletion protection

* Set `deletion_protection = false` in `acct_x830_uat/services/identity-service/rds.tf` (or equivalent)
* Apply; verify plan shows exactly 1 change: `deletion_protection: true → false`

### Stage 2 — Destroy RDS and rotation infra

* Remove `rds.tf` and related Lambda rotation, `db_credentials` secret, rotation IAM, CW alarm, CW dashboard from the UAT identity-service module
* Apply; Terraform takes final snapshot before destroying (`skip_final_snapshot = false`)

**Expected destroys:**

* `aws_db_instance.identity`
* `aws_db_subnet_group.identity`
* `aws_db_parameter_group.identity_pg15`
* `aws_security_group.identity_rds`
* `aws_lambda_function.rotate_identity_db`
* `aws_iam_role.rotation_lambda` + policies
* `aws_secretsmanager_secret.db_credentials` + rotation
* `aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm.rotation_lambda_errors`
* `aws_cloudwatch_dashboard.identity_secret_rotation`

**Verify post-apply:** `identity-service` and `admin-identity-service` ECS services still healthy (they use `platform-uat`, unaffected).

title: Destroy identity-prod RDS — orphaned identity-service instance (change window required)
description:
Follow-on to [DO-705](https://linear.app/twenty/issue/DO-705/destroy-identity-dev-rds-after-eric-mai-sign-off) (dev destroy, PR #524) and [DO-734](https://linear.app/twenty/issue/DO-734/destroy-identity-uat-rds-orphaned-identity-service-instance-multi) (UAT destroy). `identity-prod` is confirmed orphaned — 0 `DatabaseConnections` over 7+ days. The identity-service ECS task def routes `HT_IDENTITY_APP_DATABASE_URL` to `platform-prod`, not this instance.

**Requires a scheduled change window** given prod risk. Coordinate timing before applying Stage 2.

**Two-stage Terraform destroy (same pattern as** [DO-705](https://linear.app/twenty/issue/DO-705/destroy-identity-dev-rds-after-eric-mai-sign-off)**):**

### Stage 1 — Disable deletion protection

* Set `deletion_protection = false` in `acct_x830_prod/services/identity-service/rds.tf` (or equivalent)
* Apply; verify plan shows exactly 1 change: `deletion_protection: true → false`

### Stage 2 — Destroy RDS and rotation infra (change window)

* Remove `rds.tf` and related Lambda rotation, `db_credentials` secret, rotation IAM, CW alarm, CW dashboard from the prod identity-service module
* Apply; Terraform takes final snapshot before destroying (`skip_final_snapshot = false`)

**Expected destroys:**

* `aws_db_instance.identity`
* `aws_db_subnet_group.identity`
* `aws_db_parameter_group.identity_pg15`
* `aws_security_group.identity_rds`
* `aws_lambda_function.rotate_identity_db`
* `aws_iam_role.rotation_lambda` + policies
* `aws_secretsmanager_secret.db_credentials` + rotation
* `aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm.rotation_lambda_errors`
* `aws_cloudwatch_dashboard.identity_secret_rotation`

**Verify post-apply:** `identity-service` and `admin-identity-service` ECS services still healthy (they use `platform-prod`, unaffected). Monitor for 15 min post-apply.

title: terraform-modules: module directory and naming foundation
description:
Establish the directory structure, naming conventions, and data tier foundation for terraform-modules before the first atom build-out begins.

## Context

Design decisions locked in a grill-with-docs session (2026-05-29):

* Atoms and molecules are grouped by provider subdir: `modules/atoms/aws/`, `modules/atoms/github/`, `modules/molecules/aws/`, etc.
* A new `modules/data/` tier holds data-source-only modules (no resources): `metadata`, `assume-role-policies`, `cidrs`
* Module directory names use hyphens; `s3_bucket` is the one existing violation

ADRs written: 0001 (provider-grouped dirs), 0002 (data tier), 0003 (IAM principal molecules)
CONTEXT.md created at repo root.

## Sub-issues

See children for individual work items.

title: Restructure atoms and molecules to provider-grouped directory layout
description:
Move all existing atoms and molecules into provider-grouped subdirectories per ADR-0001.

## Changes

**AWS atoms** → `modules/atoms/aws/`

* `modules/atoms/cloudwatch-metric-alarm` → `modules/atoms/aws/cloudwatch-metric-alarm`
* `modules/atoms/s3_bucket` → `modules/atoms/aws/s3-bucket` (rename too)
* `modules/atoms/sns-topic` → `modules/atoms/aws/sns-topic`

**GitHub atoms** → `modules/atoms/github/`

* `modules/atoms/github-branch-protection` → `modules/atoms/github/branch-protection`
* `modules/atoms/github-branch-ruleset` → `modules/atoms/github/branch-ruleset`
* `modules/atoms/github-repository` → `modules/atoms/github/repository`
* `modules/atoms/github-repository-collaborator` → `modules/atoms/github/repository-collaborator`
* `modules/atoms/github-team-repository` → `modules/atoms/github/team-repository`

**Molecules** → provider subdirs

* `modules/molecules/cloudwatch-email-alarm` → `modules/molecules/aws/cloudwatch-email-alarm`
* `modules/molecules/github-managed-repo` → `modules/molecules/github/managed-repo`

Fix any internal `source` references in molecules that point to sibling atoms. Verify `pre-commit run --all-files` passes after restructure.

No consumers reference these paths yet — zero breakage risk.

title: Build modules/data/aws/metadata data module
description:
Create `modules/data/aws/metadata` — a data-only module that surfaces common AWS account identity values so consumers don't repeat the same data sources in every [helpers.tf](<http://helpers.tf>).

## Outputs

* `account_id` — from `data.aws_caller_identity.current`
* `account_alias` — from `data.aws_iam_account_alias.current`
* `partition` — from `data.aws_partition.current`
* `region` — from `data.aws_region.current`

## Files

* `terraform.tf` — required_version + aws provider constraint
* `outputs.tf` — all four outputs with descriptions
* `README.md` — terraform-docs generated

## Consumer usage

```hcl
module "metadata" {
  source = "git::https://github.com/isapp/terraform-modules?ref=modules/data/aws/metadata/v1.0.0"
}
# then: module.metadata.account_id, module.metadata.region, etc.
```

title: Build modules/data/aws/assume-role-policies data module
description:
Create `modules/data/aws/assume-role-policies` — pre-built `aws_iam_policy_document` trust policies for common AWS services. Trust policies only (who can assume the role) — no permission policies.

## Outputs (minimum viable set)

* `ecs_tasks` — trust policy for `ecs-tasks.amazonaws.com`
* `lambda` — trust policy for `lambda.amazonaws.com`
* `states` — trust policy for `states.amazonaws.com`
* `ec2` — trust policy for `ec2.amazonaws.com`

Add further services as needed when IAM molecules are built.

## Files

* `terraform.tf` — required_version + aws provider constraint
* `outputs.tf` — one output per service, all descriptions
* `README.md` — terraform-docs generated

## Consumer usage

```hcl
module "policies" {
  source = "git::https://github.com/isapp/terraform-modules?ref=modules/data/aws/assume-role-policies/v1.0.0"
}

module "ecs_task_role" {
  source             = ".../aws/iam-role"
  assume_role_policy = module.policies.ecs_tasks
  ...
}
```

title: Complete modules/data/aws/cidrs with GovCloud CIDRs
description:
Add GovCloud environment CIDR entries to `modules/data/aws/cidrs/locals.tf`.

Commercial CIDRs are already live-verified and committed (dev=10.1, stg=10.2, uat=10.3, prod=10.4). GovCloud CIDRs were not confirmed due to expired SSO at time of initial build.

## Steps

1. Re-auth GovCloud SSO: `aws sso login --profile gov-main-276964819952`
2. Query VPCs in `us-gov-west-1` for profiles: `gov-main`, `gov-sandbox`, `gov-mgmt`, `gov-logs`
3. Verify subnet layout follows the same /22 public + /20 private per-AZ pattern
4. Add `gov_main`, `gov_sandbox` (and others as applicable) entries to `locals.tf` and `outputs.tf`
5. Also assess `snowplow-066934265599` — determine if it needs a CIDR entry

## Deferred because

GovCloud SSO token was expired during initial cidrs module build on 2026-05-29.

Build custom tflint ruleset for terraform-modules (isapp/tflint-ruleset-ht)
description:
## Overview

Build a custom tflint ruleset published at `isapp/tflint-ruleset-ht` that enforces the atomic module conventions defined in `CLAUDE.md` for `isapp/terraform-modules`.

## Rules to Implement

| Rule | Description |
| -- | -- |
| `variable_location` | All `variable` blocks must be in `inputs.tf`, not any other file |
| `variable_order` | Variables must be sorted A–Z by name within each section (required section and defaults section independently) |
| `variable_field_order` | Within each variable block, field order must be: `type`, `default`, `description` |
| `variable_section_order` | Required variables (no `default`) must appear before the `DEFAULTS` separator; variables with `default` must appear after it |
| `key_attributes_first` | Key-identifying resource attributes (e.g. `bucket`, `name`) must appear before other attributes |

## [inputs.tf](<http://inputs.tf>) Structure Convention

Required variables (no `default`) are grouped at the top of `inputs.tf`. A visual separator divides them from optional variables. Optional variables follow the separator, sorted A–Z.

```hcl
variable "bucket" {
  type        = string
  description = "The name of the bucket. Must be globally unique."
}

###############################################
#               DEFAULTS                      #
###############################################

variable "force_destroy" {
  type        = bool
  default     = false
  description = "If true, all objects will be deleted from the bucket when the bucket is destroyed."
}
```

The `variable_section_order` rule enforces:

* Any variable without a `default` must appear before the separator comment block
* Any variable with a `default` must appear after the separator comment block
* The separator must be present if there are both required and optional variables

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Ruleset repo exists at `https://github.com/isapp/tflint-ruleset-ht`
- [ ] All 5 rules implemented and tested
- [ ] Ruleset installable via `.tflint.hcl` plugin block
- [ ] README documents each rule with pass/fail examples
- [ ] Integrated into `.tflint.hcl` in `terraform-modules`

## References

* Repo: [https://github.com/isapp/tflint-ruleset-ht](<https://github.com/isapp/tflint-ruleset-ht>)
* Reference implementation: [https://github.com/phazeight/tflint-ruleset-trusty](<https://github.com/phazeight/tflint-ruleset-trusty>)
* tflint plugin authoring: [https://github.com/terraform-linters/tflint/blob/master/docs/developer-guide/plugins.md](<https://github.com/terraform-linters/tflint/blob/master/docs/developer-guide/plugins.md>)
* Parent issue: DO-12

title: Set up pre-commit hooks for terraform-modules (fmt, validate, tflint, terraform-docs)
description:
## Overview

Configure pre-commit hooks in `isapp/terraform-modules` to enforce code quality gates on every commit and in CI.

## Hooks to Configure

| Hook | Source | Purpose |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `terraform_fmt` | `antonbabenko/pre-commit-terraform` | Auto-format all `.tf` files |
| `terraform_validate` | `antonbabenko/pre-commit-terraform` | Validate module syntax |
| `terraform_tflint` | `antonbabenko/pre-commit-terraform` | Run tflint with `isapp/tflint-ruleset-ht` |
| `terraform_docs` | `antonbabenko/pre-commit-terraform` | Auto-regenerate `README.md` docs sections |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [X] `.pre-commit-config.yaml` committed to `terraform-modules`
- [X] All hooks run cleanly against the existing `atoms/aws/s3-bucket` module
- [X] Pre-commit also runs in GitHub Actions CI on every PR
- [X] Developer setup instructions added to `CLAUDE.md`

## References

* [https://github.com/antonbabenko/pre-commit-terraform](<https://github.com/antonbabenko/pre-commit-terraform>)
* Parent issue: DO-12

title: Integrate terraform-docs for auto-generated README inputs/outputs per module
description:
## Overview

Integrate `terraform-docs` into `isapp/terraform-modules` so that each module's `README.md` has an auto-generated inputs/outputs table kept in sync with the module's source.

## Implementation

* Add a `.terraform-docs.yml` config file at the repo root defining output format and sort order
* Each module `README.md` contains `<!-- BEGIN_TF_DOCS -->` / `<!-- END_TF_DOCS -->` markers
* terraform-docs is run via the `terraform_docs` pre-commit hook (see pre-commit sub-issue)
* CI enforces that `README.md` is up to date (fails PR if docs are stale)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [X] `.terraform-docs.yml` committed to repo root
- [X] `atoms/aws/s3-bucket/README.md` has a fully generated inputs/outputs table
- [X] Pre-commit hook regenerates docs automatically
- [X] CI step fails if docs are out of date

## References

* [https://terraform-docs.io/](<https://terraform-docs.io/>)
* [https://github.com/terraform-docs/terraform-docs](<https://github.com/terraform-docs/terraform-docs>)
* Parent issue: [DO-12](https://linear.app/twenty/issue/DO-12/set-up-terraform-module-releaser-monorepo-with-github-actions-in-ht)
